correctness.rationale: By consistency the residual lies in range(A), where B=AA^T has two positive levels. Normalize them to kappa and 1, leaving alpha B unchanged, and let e_k be the high-to-low spectral energy ratio. The first Rayleigh step inverts e_0. Substituting the residual difference into the RD quotient gives (1+kappa² e_(k−1))/(1+kappa³ e_(k−1)) in normalized units. For mixed data both filters remain nonzero. With z_k=log(kappa²e_k), their squared ratio gives z_(k+1)=z_k−2z_(k−1) and z_0+z_1=4 log(kappa)>0. The roots are sqrt(2) times unit rotations by ±theta, with π/3<theta<π/2. Four successive phase samples have all circular gaps below π, so compactness supplies a uniform positive and negative cosine excursion, bounded away from zero, in each such block. The high- and low-mode negative log multipliers are respectively [z_(k−1)]_+ and [−z_(k−1)]_+ up to bounded errors. Summing the last four excursions bounds each negative log mode norm from below by a positive constant times 2^(k/2) and summing the geometric majorant bounds it above at that scale; O(k) errors are negligible. The fixed first-step log corrections can depend on the start, so the bound on the remainder can be written O_kappa(k)+O_kappa,e0(1). Orthogonality transfers the result, with start-dependent constants, to the residual norm. A zero residual is already solved, and either pure mode is annihilated in the first step. This is not a consecutive-step Q-rate.
